cls: Vaccine - bacterial capsular polysaccharide (Salmonella Typhi Vi antigen)
quick: A single 0.5 mL (25 microgram) intramuscular dose; re-vaccinate every ~2-3 years if continued exposure
Use only if clearly needed; inactivated polysaccharide vaccine - give if exposure risk is high
Considered compatible; may be given to breastfeeding women when indicated
Observe for immediate hypersensitivity after injection; expected protection is partial
summary: Purified Vi polysaccharide typhoid vaccine is an injectable, inactivated vaccine made from the purified Vi capsular polysaccharide of Salmonella Typhi. A single intramuscular dose provides partial protection (about 50-70%) against typhoid fever and is used mainly for travelers to endemic areas and other at-risk individuals. It is given to people aged 2 years and older and requires periodic boosting.
indications: Active immunization against typhoid fever caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi
For travelers to endemic areas, household contacts of carriers, and laboratory/at-risk workers

dosage.n: Give at least ~2 weeks before expected exposure

admin: Administer intramuscularly (deltoid in adults/older children; anterolateral thigh in young children)
Give at least 2 weeks before potential exposure to allow protective antibody development
Not recommended for routine use in children under 2 years (poor polysaccharide response)
Have facilities to manage an acute allergic reaction available
moa: The vaccine contains purified Vi capsular polysaccharide of Salmonella Typhi. It induces a T-cell-independent B-cell response producing anti-Vi IgG antibodies that promote opsonization and complement-mediated killing of the organism, conferring partial (about 50-70%) protection against typhoid fever.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any vaccine component or a prior dose
Acute moderate or severe febrile illness (defer until recovery)

preg: This is an inactivated polysaccharide vaccine. There are limited data in pregnancy; give only if the risk of typhoid exposure is substantial and clearly outweighs any theoretical risk.
lact: Considered compatible with breastfeeding; the vaccine may be given to nursing mothers when indicated.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy (corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) may blunt the antibody response
minor: Can be co-administered with most other travel vaccines at separate sites

common: Injection-site pain, redness, swelling, or induration

monitoring: Observation for immediate allergic reaction after administration
Awareness that protection is partial - continue food/water precautions
counsel: This vaccine gives partial protection - still follow safe food and water practices when traveling
Get vaccinated at least 2 weeks before travel to an endemic area
A booster is needed roughly every 2-3 years with continued exposure
Mild soreness, low fever, or tiredness for a day or two is expected
Seek urgent care for any difficulty breathing, swelling, or rash soon after the injection
pk: Protective anti-Vi antibody develops over about 1-2 weeks
Peak antibody titers around 2-4 weeks after vaccination
Not applicable (immune response, not a drug)
Protection roughly 2-3 years; boost with continued exposure
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: Single-dose injectable Vi polysaccharide gives ~50-70% protection - emphasize food/water hygiene as well
Poor immunogenicity under 2 years; newer Vi-conjugate (TCV) vaccines work in infants and give longer protection
Inactivated polysaccharide - cannot cause typhoid; can be given to immunocompromised (with reduced response)
NOTE: this is a biologic (regulated under a BLA/national authority) and is not in the openFDA drug-label dataset; content follows WHO position paper and manufacturer prescribing information
missed: For a missed booster dose, administer it as soon as practical if exposure risk continues; no need to restart the series - a single dose re-establishes protection.
overdose: Overdose is not applicable to a single standardized vaccine dose. Inadvertent extra dosing is not expected to cause harm beyond increased local/systemic reactogenicity; manage symptomatically.
